textPlacement.assessment: Pass for this exact text and placement. The recognizable sleep title, both short topic rows and the full entry treat settling as responsive support, retain the baby’s and adult’s readiness, and avoid grading feeding, rocking or waking. The short row states the limits of adult control and frames a familiar routine as an option. The full entry’s source-tension paragraph is more formal than the surrounding prose, but it serves a reader-facing purpose without replacing the warm account with a prohibition. The entry describes the authors’ responsive perspective without converting disputed sleeping-arrangement examples or their detailed settling protocols into care instructions.
textPlacement.ageAndPlacement: The 6–9-month browse label is qualified by a first-year book context with no required age for independent settling, individual tired signs and adult readiness. Both Everyday care and Connection & feelings rows preserve their own source attribution and nonperformance framing.

issues.surface: RENDERED_SURFACES.json: 6-9.baby-pacifier entryText, Age, interest & context / In the book
issues.finding: “Infant-wide discussion; this summary does not use the book’s removal-age preference as a deadline.” describes an editorial omission instead of directly orienting the reader. The unspecified removal-age preference introduces an unanswered age concern into the public age note, making an otherwise measured entry sound like internal review prose.
issues.requiredCorrection: Replace the editorial-process clause with direct source-faithful age/situation context. Keep the infant-wide scope and avoid presenting a removal preference as a deadline; do not introduce a removal method or an unsupported age rule merely to explain the omission.

textPlacement.assessment: Revise one age-context sentence. The title clearly identifies pacifiers and its attribution to the book is appropriate for this source-sensitive perspective. Both short rows carry the source’s qualified discouragement, possible SIDS-risk reduction and allowance for limited settling/sleep use together. The detail gives the communication concern without an absolute ban or a fabricated removal procedure. The public bookAge sentence, however, shifts into a description of what this summary omitted and raises an unnamed removal-age preference; it needs direct reader-facing age context.
textPlacement.ageAndPlacement: Infant-wide framing is appropriate in the 6–9-month browse band. The selected situation and family use are preferable to an invented readiness test. The open issue affects the full entry’s Age, interest & context section; neither topic row has the same wording problem.

issues.surface: RENDERED_SURFACES.json: 6-9.baby-sharing topicRows[connection-feelings], topicRows[play-discovery], and entryText title/summary
issues.finding: The summary says another child reaches for the baby’s object, then says to put “that wish” into words and help “them” finish “their turn.” Those references can identify the reaching child instead of the baby who is still using the object. The title “Help a turn last” also implies prolonging a turn, whereas the source asks the adult to notice whether this baby actually wants to continue. The full detail permits moving on, but neither short row contains that clarification.
issues.requiredCorrection: Make the short surface explicitly identify the baby who may want to finish and the other child who is reaching. Preserve the source’s tentative interpretation and the possibility that the baby is content to move on. Use a recognizable sharing/turn-taking title that does not imply an adult goal of lengthening the turn. Check the rewritten title and summary together in both topic rows.

textPlacement.assessment: Revise the short-facing description of whose wish and turn the adult supports. The full entry usefully allows a young baby to move on or hold on, and covers the reciprocal situation without forcing sharing. The short summary’s “that wish” and “them” can instead refer to the reaching child, leaving the reader unsure whose continued turn is being supported. Its title also suggests making a turn last rather than recognizing the baby’s actual interest. Because both topic rows contain only this title and summary, the detail cannot resolve their ambiguity.
textPlacement.ageAndPlacement: The full age context distinguishes first-year exploration from ownership/sharing concepts discussed around 12–16 months. Connection & feelings and Play & discovery are appropriate topics once the short row clearly identifies the actors and preserves the baby’s option to move on.
